summary.headline: An excellent business, priced for growth that Sri Lankan interest rates don't support
summary.text: Dialog Axiata (DIAL.N0000) is Sri Lanka's dominant telecom company: about 64% of mobile users, the largest broadband and pay-TV operator, the first 5G network, low debt and a AAA local credit rating. It is getting better: profit for the September 2026 quarter rose 62% to Rs 9.24bn (EPS Rs 1.00), and trailing EPS is now about Rs 3.74, against Rs 2.26 for 2025. But at Rs 49.70 (CSE close, 11 November 2026) the price has run ahead even of that. It earns 7.5% on the price (P/E 13.3x) while 10-year government bonds pay about 12.4%, and to justify Rs 49.70 its free cash flow would need to grow about 12% a year for five years. Four methods put fair value at about Rs 32 (Rs 31 last time), so the price is about 55% above it; even my bull case (Rs 47) is below today's price. I'd buy at up to about Rs 27.20 and treat under Rs 24 as a strong buy. On peer multiples (Sri Lanka Telecom and regional telecoms at roughly 15–16x earnings) it looks fairly priced, which is why brokers are more positive; the gap is about interest rates, not the business.

quality.reason: Dominant, cash-generative and lightly indebted; the one failure is the 2022 loss in the rupee crisis.

tests.label: Net debt no more than equity (and no more than 3x EBITDA)
tests.note: Including leases, June 2026. USD debt cut to Rs 5.6bn from Rs 34.9bn.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: Rs 33.4bn loss when the rupee collapsed; profitable every year since. Exchange gains/losses still swing quarterly profit by up to Rs 0.9bn.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends (cash conversion 70%+ over 3 years)
tests.note: Operating cash flow Rs 136bn against Rs 53bn of profit in 2023–2025; about 75% of profit paid out.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of four methods 30/50/20. Confidence is medium, so the standard 15% / 25% margins apply.

highlights.title: September 2026 quarter (press reports; report not yet in the folder)
highlights.text: Revenue rose 6.2% to Rs 48.54bn and profit 62% to Rs 9.24bn (EPS Rs 1.00 against Rs 0.62), despite a Rs 0.92bn exchange loss. Net finance costs fell 25%. A third Rs 0.70 interim dividend was declared.

highlights.title: First half of 2026 (reviewed by the auditors)
highlights.text: Revenue up 9% to Rs 95.5bn; profit Rs 19.3bn against Rs 9.2bn (EPS Rs 2.10 against Rs 1.00). Gross margin 56.8% (51.8%) as direct costs fell; finance costs fell and there was a Rs 0.5bn exchange gain.

highlights.title: 5G spending is starting
highlights.text: Dialog won 5G spectrum in December 2025. Capex committed in H1 2026 was Rs 24.6bn (19% of revenue) against Rs 11.0bn a year earlier, and contracted capex rose to Rs 16.9bn from Rs 6.3bn. Free cash flow will be lower in the second half.

highlights.title: Correction to the last analysis
highlights.text: The final dividend for 2025 was Rs 1.50, not Rs 2.20: the Rs 2.20 in the June interim is the Rs 1.50 final plus the first Rs 0.70 interim for 2026. The yield was right in total but mislabelled.

methodReadings.reading: 5.1x NAV. NAV understates a telecom, whose value is its network, spectrum and customers, so I give it no direct weight.
Excellent, but partly because the 2022 loss and dividends shrank equity; it should fade as equity rebuilds and 5G is depreciated.
Earnings yield 7.5% against a 12.4% government bond. Dialog's own year-end P/E averaged about 7.6x in 2021–2025 (excluding 2022).
Rs 0.70 a quarter; about 75% of profit paid out. After 15% withholding tax, about 4.8%.
Strong, but 5G capex (Rs 16.9bn contracted) will absorb more cash in 2026–2027.
On peer P/Es Dialog would be worth Rs 52–60. Peers' P/Es don't account for Sri Lanka's 12.4% bond yield, so I use them as a check, not a method.

modelsNote: A steady cash generator, so the DCF carries real weight, alongside P/E, dividends and residual income. The dividend and residual-income methods are lower because Dialog pays most profit out and keeps a small book value.

scenarios.common: 10-year government bond about 12.4% (9 Nov 2026), one-year T-bill about 9.1%, policy rate 8.75% (raised in May 2026). Base cost of equity = bond + about 4 points for a defensive, AAA-rated market leader. Base FCFE assumes capex of about 15% of revenue once 5G spending settles.

sensitivity.title: DCF base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Even the most generous corner (Rs 51.90) only just reaches today's price.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 14,080 in total, against Rs 24,850 at Rs 49.70.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 27.20 needs about a 45% fall. The share was below that until late 2025 (2025 close Rs 29.80) and its 2026 low was Rs 30.10 (April–June). A return there would probably take a market fall or higher interest rates.

higher: Interest rates falling (each point off the cost of equity adds about Rs 4–5 a share).
5G and home broadband lifting revenue growth well above 6% without capex staying near 19% of revenue.
Margins holding near 55% as energy costs ease.
A higher dividend (Rs 0.80+ a quarter) sustained.
lower: 5G capex absorbing cash and cutting dividends.
Loss of the 2% revenue-based tax deal with the BOI (the company would face 30% tax on profit).
Another rupee crisis (2022: a Rs 33bn loss).
Price competition from SLT-Mobitel and Hutch, or regulator-imposed tariff cuts.
Foreign investors continuing to sell (Rs 1.0bn net sold on 10 November).

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the interim reports to June 2026, plus September-quarter headline figures from press reports; the full September report wasn't in the folder. Figures for the 12 months to September 2026 are estimates. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: about 55% above fair value of Rs 32.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 49.70: About −3% a year over three years: dividends 5.6% + growth 5% − about 13.6% a year if the price moved to fair value. After 15% dividend tax and brokerage, about −4%.
Decision box.Downside / upside: Bear case −57% (Rs 21.40); bull case −6% (Rs 46.80). Even the bull case is below today's price.
Decision box.What the price assumes: About 12% a year free-cash-flow growth for five years (base case 6%), or a cost of equity of 14.7%, only 2.3 points above government bonds.
Decision box.Confidence: Medium: the methods give Rs 23–42 in the base case; the business is predictable but 2022 showed how a rupee crisis can hit it.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Medium confidence: buy 15% below fair value (Rs 27.20), strong buy 25% below (Rs 24.00).

Business and moat.What it does: Mobile (78% of H1 2026 revenue), fixed and home broadband via Dialog Broadband Networks (15%), and pay TV via Dialog Television (8%). Also digital payments (eZ Cash), data centres and a finance company.
Business and moat.Segment profit, H1 2026: Mobile Rs 20.0bn, fixed/broadband Rs 5.4bn, TV Rs 0.4bn of operating profit.
Business and moat.Market position: About 64% of mobile subscribers (19.6 million) after merging with Airtel Lanka in 2024; 22.3 million subscribers in total; largest pay-TV operator (1.6 million+). Competitors: SLT-Mobitel (state-controlled) and Hutch.
Business and moat.Moat: Wide: scale in a three-player market, the largest network, 5G spectrum won in December 2025 (100 MHz at 3.5 GHz, 200 MHz at 27 GHz), the strongest brand, and a tax deal competitors don't have.
Business and moat.Growth drivers: Data and home-broadband demand, price increases, 5G (1.5 million+ 5G users), enterprise and digital services. The low-margin international 'hubbing' business has been scaled down.
Business and moat.Customer and supplier concentration: Millions of retail customers; key suppliers are network-equipment vendors and the energy grid.
Business and moat.Tax advantage: The company pays a 2% revenue-based tax under its BOI agreement instead of 30% on profit; its broadband and TV subsidiaries pay 15% and 20%.

Management and governance.Ownership: Axiata Group (Malaysia) 73.75%, Bharti Airtel 10.36%, EPF 2.90%. Public float 15.85%, of which foreign investors held 53% at end-2025.
Management and governance.Track record: Delivered Rs 5.5bn of cost savings in 2025, completed the Airtel merger, cut USD debt from Rs 34.9bn to Rs 5.6bn, and paid above its 50% minimum payout. Rated OK.
Management and governance.Capital allocation: About 75% of profit paid out; capex being raised for 5G; simplifying the group by moving dormant subsidiaries under one holding company; sold 20% of Digital Health in October 2026.
Management and governance.Related parties: Head-office charges to Axiata Rs 0.41bn in 2025 (Rs 1.1bn in 2024). A Rs 1.06bn impairment on money owed by affiliates in 2025: watch.
Management and governance.Auditor: Deloitte; clean opinion for 2025. Key audit matters: Rs 19.8bn of goodwill impairment testing, and mobile revenue recognition. The June 2026 interim was reviewed.
Management and governance.Director dealings: The CEO, Supun Weerasinghe, holds 4.26 million shares; no other directors hold shares directly.
Management and governance.Legal: A Rs 1.63bn customs dispute (Dialog Broadband Networks) is still in the Court of Appeal.

Accounting quality.Underlying earnings: Exchange losses net of gains of about Rs 0.75bn over the 12 months to September 2026 removed: underlying EPS about Rs 3.82 against reported Rs 3.74.
Accounting quality.Restatements: 2024 figures were restated in the 2025 accounts (December 2025 interim, note 17).
Accounting quality.Revaluations: None: property and equipment are carried at cost, so NAV isn't inflated.
Accounting quality.To check: The 'provision for other liabilities' (asset retirement obligations) jumped from Rs 4.96bn to Rs 9.14bn in January–March 2026 with no explanation in the interim reports.

Peer and history comparison.Sri Lanka Telecom (SLTL.N0000): P/E about 15–18x, P/B about 1.5x, ROE about 11%, dividend yield about 1%, EV/EBITDA about 5x (web data from June 2026; dates vary).
Peer and history comparison.Dialog's own history: Year-end P/E 3.7–13.2x in 2021–2025 (average about 7.6x excluding 2022); P/B 1.0–3.0x. Today's 13.3x and 5.1x are at the top of its range.
Peer and history comparison.Reading: Cheap against peers on P/E, expensive against its own history and against Sri Lankan bond yields.

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: policy rate raised to 8.75% in May 2026; 10-year bond about 12.4%. A yield stock like Dialog loses value when rates rise.
Sri Lanka checks.Rupee: Watch: rupee down 6.7% against the dollar this year (6 Nov). Network equipment, energy and roaming are dollar-linked; dollar debt is now small (Rs 5.6bn). Exchange loss Rs 0.92bn in the September quarter.
Sri Lanka checks.Tax and regulation: Risk: the 2% revenue tax depends on the BOI agreement; telecom levies and tariff approvals by the regulator (TRCSL); the 2027 budget was being finalised in November 2026.
Sri Lanka checks.Dependence on the state: OK: customers are households and businesses, not the government.
Sri Lanka checks.Energy and weather: Watch: high energy costs from the Middle East conflict; Cyclone Ditwah disrupted the network in late 2025.
Sri Lanka checks.Liquidity: OK: one of the most traded shares on the CSE; 500 shares (about Rs 24,850) are easy to buy or sell.
Sri Lanka checks.Free float and control: Watch: only 15.85% free float; Axiata controls the company.
Sri Lanka checks.Catalysts: Ex-dividend Rs 0.70 on 20 November (paid 10 December); 2025/26 full-year results due early February 2027; 5G rollout and capex; any change in Axiata's stake.
Sri Lanka checks.ESG: OK: no major controversies found; energy use and carbon footprint are the main issues.
Sri Lanka checks.Going concern / audit: OK: clean audit opinion, AAA(lka) rating from Fitch.

Crisis stress test (2022-style).Scenario: Rupee falls 40%, interest rates up 10 points, demand down 5%.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Likely effect (rough estimate): Exchange loss on dollar debt about Rs 4bn; extra interest about Rs 7bn a year on Rs 71bn of local borrowings; higher dollar costs. Profit could fall from about Rs 35bn to about Rs 15–20bn.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Survival: Survives comfortably: low debt, AAA rating and a strong parent. Dividends would probably be cut, and the share price could halve (in 2022 it fell to Rs 8.50 and the P/E collapsed).

Portfolio fit.Cost of 500 shares: About Rs 24,850 now; about Rs 13,600 at the buy price.
Portfolio fit.Overlap: None with other companies on the site; it is the site's only telecom.
Portfolio fit.Note: Shown for information, not as advice on how much to hold.

Broker view.HNB Stockbrokers (9 Nov 2026): Moderate buy, target Rs 55, against my fair value of Rs 32.
Broker view.Why we differ: The broker's target is close to peer P/E multiples (about 15x); my methods discount future cash at about 16.5% because Sri Lankan bonds yield 12.4%. If rates fall, the gap narrows.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: Dominant market leader with a wide moat, high returns, strong cash flow, low debt and a 5–7% dividend.
Investment case and sell rules.The case is broken if: Market share falls clearly below 60%; the BOI tax deal ends; 5G capex forces a dividend cut; or a rupee crisis returns.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 41.60: today's price is above this); the case breaks; or a clearly better opportunity appears.

Key ratios (five-year trend).DuPont (2025): Net margin 11.6% × asset turnover 0.61 × leverage 3.5 ≈ ROE 23–25%
Key ratios (five-year trend).EPS: 2021 Rs 2.08 · 2022 −Rs 4.06 · 2023 Rs 2.44 · 2024 Rs 1.43 · 2025 Rs 2.26 · 12 months to Sep 2026 Rs 3.74 (underlying, without exchange gains/losses, Rs 3.82)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Dividend cover / payout: Cover about 1.3x; payout about 75% (policy minimum 50%; 66% for 2025)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Free cash flow to equity (after interest: 2024 Rs 10.9bn · 2025 Rs 33.7bn · 12 months to Jun 2026 Rs 45.3bn (Rs 4.92 a share)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Accruals: Low: operating cash flow is far above profit because depreciation is large
Key ratios (five-year trend).Inventory / receivable / payable days (2: 8 / 77 / 292 days; cash conversion cycle about −208 days (customers prepay and suppliers, including capex suppliers, are paid late)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Current ratio / quick ratio: Jun 2026 0.47 / 0.46 (normal for a telecom with prepaid customers)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Debt due within a year: 73% of borrowings (Rs 52.3bn of Rs 71.3bn), mostly revolving local bank loans and overdrafts
Key ratios (five-year trend).Share count change: +13% in 2024 (shares issued to Bharti Airtel for Airtel Lanka); none since
Key ratios (five-year trend).EV/EBITDA and EV/EBIT: 5.5x and 11.0x (EV Rs 521bn; EBITDA and EBIT for the 12 months to June 2026)
Key ratios (five-year trend).PEG: About 2.6 on 5% expected growth (0.9 on the 15% a year EPS recovery since 2023, which won't repeat)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Earnings yield vs 10-year bond: 7.5% vs about 12.4%: the share earns 4.9 points less than a government bond
Key ratios (five-year trend).FCF yield: 9.9% on the 12 months to June 2026 (flattered by low capex paid in H1 2026; about 9.4% on my normalised Rs 43bn)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Dividend yield: 5.6% on Rs 2.80 a year (four quarterly Rs 0.70s); 7.2% on the Rs 3.60 declared over the last 12 months including the 2025 final
Key ratios (five-year trend).Graham number: Rs 28.50 (√(22.5 × EPS 3.74 × NAV 9.68)); understates high-return businesses like Dialog
Key ratios (five-year trend).Piotroski F-score (2025): 8 of 9: strong (only the current ratio got worse)
Key ratios (five-year trend).Altman Z''-score (Jun 2026): 0.48, which reads as 'distress', but it isn't meaningful here: the formula penalises negative working capital, which is normal for telecoms (prepaid customers, long supplier terms). Fitch rates Dialog AAA(lka).

What this analysis doesn't cover: The full September 2026 interim report: only press-reported headline figures were used. Please add it to the dialog folder.
The reason for the Rs 4.2bn jump in asset-retirement provisions in early 2026.
Exact 5G spectrum cost and capex guidance for 2026–2027 (not disclosed in the reports read).
Subscriber and market-share figures after December 2025.
Peer figures for Sri Lanka Telecom come from web data with mixed dates; its own reports weren't read.
fullText:
Summary: Dialog Axiata (DIAL.N0000) is Sri Lanka's dominant telecom company: about 64% of mobile users, the largest broadband and pay-TV operator, the first 5G network, low debt and a AAA local credit rating. It is getting better: profit for the September 2026 quarter rose 62% to Rs 9.24bn (EPS Rs 1.00), and trailing EPS is now about Rs 3.74, against Rs 2.26 for 2025. But at Rs 49.70 (CSE close, 11 November 2026) the price has run ahead even of that. It earns 7.5% on the price (P/E 13.3x) while 10-year government bonds pay about 12.4%, and to justify Rs 49.70 its free cash flow would need to grow about 12% a year for five years. Four methods put fair value at about Rs 32 (Rs 31 last time), so the price is about 55% above it; even my bull case (Rs 47) is below today's price. I'd buy at up to about Rs 27.20 and treat under Rs 24 as a strong buy. On peer multiples (Sri Lanka Telecom and regional telecoms at roughly 15–16x earnings) it looks fairly priced, which is why brokers are more positive; the gap is about interest rates, not the business.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 49.70 (CSE close, 11 November 2026). It closed September at Rs 45.80 and traded between Rs 30.10 and Rs 48.40 in April–June 2026; it closed 2025 at Rs 29.80 and 2024 at Rs 11.70.
September 2026 quarter (press reports): revenue Rs 48.54bn (up 6.2%), profit Rs 9.24bn (up 62%), EPS Rs 1.00 (Rs 0.62), exchange loss Rs 0.92bn, third interim dividend Rs 0.70.
First half of 2026 (reviewed): revenue Rs 95.5bn (up 9%), gross margin 56.8%, profit Rs 19.3bn, EPS Rs 2.10 (Rs 1.00), operating cash flow Rs 46.4bn, free cash flow about Rs 32bn.
2025 (audited): revenue Rs 179.6bn, EBITDA Rs 86.0bn (47.9% margin), profit Rs 20.8bn, EPS Rs 2.26, ROE 23%, ROCE 19.8%, dividend Rs 1.50, net debt 0.64x EBITDA.
12 months to September 2026: EPS about Rs 3.74 (Rs 3.82 without exchange gains and losses). NAV Rs 9.68 (June).

Decision box
Fair value about Rs 32; price about 55% above it. Expected return at today's price about −3% a year over three years, against a one-year T-bill of about 9.1%. Bear case −57%, bull case −6%. The price assumes about 12% a year free-cash-flow growth for five years, or a cost of equity of 14.7%. Confidence medium, so buy at up to Rs 27.20 (−15%) and strong buy under Rs 24.00 (−25%).

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
FCFE DCF | 25.7 | 41.9 | 64.2 | 41.5
P/E | 26.4 | 40.0 | 52.8 | 38.5
Dividend model | 16.2 | 25.1 | 37.8 | 25.0
Residual income | 17.4 | 23.0 | 32.2 | 23.2
Average | 21.4 | 32.5 | 46.8 | 32.0

Assumptions
Cost of equity 18% / 16.5% / 15% (bond about 12.4% plus 4 points for a defensive leader). FCFE in 2027 of Rs 34 / 43 / 50bn, growing 3% / 6% / 8% for five years and 4% / 5% / 6% after. 2027 EPS Rs 3.30 / 4.00 / 4.40 at 8 / 10 / 12 times. Dividends Rs 2.40 / 2.80 / 3.20. ROE falling from 40% to 20% / 25% / 30%.

Peers and history
Sri Lanka Telecom trades at roughly 15–18x earnings and Asian telecoms at about 16x; on those multiples Dialog would be worth Rs 52–60. But its own P/E averaged about 7.6x in 2021–2025, and its 7.5% earnings yield is well below the 12.4% government bond. HNB Stockbrokers rates it a moderate buy with a Rs 55 target.

Key ratios
ROE 23% (2025), about 39% now; ROCE 19.8%; gross margin 56%, operating margin 25%; net debt 0.67x EBITDA; interest cover 4.5x; cash conversion 2.6x; Piotroski 8/9. Altman Z'' reads as 'distress' only because telecoms run negative working capital; it isn't meaningful here.

Risks to watch
Interest rates (policy rate raised to 8.75% in May 2026), the rupee, the BOI tax deal, 5G capex, energy costs, a 15.85% free float. In a 2022-style crisis it would survive but cut dividends, and the price could halve.

Correction
The previous analysis labelled the 2025 final dividend Rs 2.20; it was Rs 1.50. The Rs 2.20 in the June interim was the final plus the first Rs 0.70 interim for 2026.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 32.00, 150 up to Rs 27.20, 150 up to Rs 24.00: average about Rs 28.20, about Rs 14,080 in total. Rs 27.20 needs about a 45% fall; it was last there in late 2025.

Sell rules
If you already hold Dialog: the price is above the sell trigger (30% above fair value, Rs 41.60). The business case itself is intact.

Business tests: 3 of 4 passed (returns, debt, cash; fails steady profit because of the 2022 loss), so it's a good business at a high price: watch list, unchanged.
